I'll walk you through both the subject line and body personalization using AMPscript. ## Subject Line The subject line renders **last** in SFMC (after the HTML and text bodies), so you can set a variable in the body and reference it in the subject. However, **text-preference subscribers skip the HTML body entirely**, so you need to either: 1. Set the variable in **both** HTML and text parts, or 2. Compute it inline in the subject line Here's the **inline approach** (safest): ``` %%=ProperCase(AttributeValue("FirstName"))=%%, your renewal is coming up ``` If `FirstName` might be missing, add a fallback: ``` %%=IIF(Empty(AttributeValue("FirstName")),"Your renewal is coming up",Concat(ProperCase(AttributeValue("FirstName")),", your renewal is coming up"))=%% ``` ## Body Copy In your **HTML body** (and duplicate in your **text body** if you have text-preference subscribers): ```html %%[ /* Calculate days until renewal */ VAR @renewalDate, @today, @daysUntil, @firstName SET @renewalDate = AttributeValue("RenewalDate") SET @today = Now() SET @firstName = ProperCase(AttributeValue("FirstName")) /* DateDiff(startDate, endDate, unit) returns endDate minus startDate */ SET @daysUntil = DateDiff(@today, @renewalDate, "D") ]%% %%[ IF @daysUntil > 0 THEN ]%%

Hi %%=v(@firstName)=%%,

Your renewal is coming up in %%=v(@daysUntil)=%% days on %%=FormatDate(@renewalDate, "MMMM D, YYYY")=%%.

%%[ ELSEIF @daysUntil == 0 THEN ]%%

Hi %%=v(@firstName)=%%,

Your renewal is today!

%%[ ELSE ]%%

Hi %%=v(@firstName)=%%,

Your renewal date has passed. Please contact us to renew your account.

%%[ ENDIF ]%% ``` ## Key Points 1. **`AttributeValue("RenewalDate")`** returns null if the field is missing (safe). A bare `%%RenewalDate%%` would terminate the send if the field doesn't exist in the sending Data Extension. 2. **`DateDiff(@today, @renewalDate, "D")`** returns a **positive** number when renewal is in the future, **negative** when it's past, and **0** if it's today. 3. **`ProperCase()`** capitalizes the first letter of each word. 4. **`v(@variable)`** outputs the variable value in AMPscript. 5. **AMPscript has no arithmetic operators** — you calculate with `Add()`, `Subtract()`, etc. Here we're just using `DateDiff()` which does the math for us. ## Testing Use **Preview and Test** in SFMC, selecting: - A subscriber **with** a future renewal date - A subscriber **with** a past renewal date - A subscriber **with** today's date - A subscriber **without** a RenewalDate value (should handle gracefully with `AttributeValue()`) **Important:** Preview against dedicated **test/seed subscribers** only — preview permanently applies changes to whichever subscriber you select, and a test send counts against your contracted volume.
